summary: Since round 3, the gateway's `returnPathPattern` also accepts `/<slug>/view` without a trailing slash, and both runs and the coverage gate pass. The Halo-origin handoff still uses the old, stricter pattern, so the two patterns now disagree. An invited visitor who opens `/<slug>/view` gets a 400 on Halo's sign-in page instead of a sign-in prompt.

findings.body: The creator gateway and the Halo-origin handoff validate the same `return` value with different patterns. `AppGateway.appPathPattern` routes `/books/view` (no trailing slash) as a view request. For an invited app with no session, the gateway redirects to `/__halo/signin?return=%2Fbooks%2Fview` (AppGateway.ts around line 165). `safeReturnPath` now accepts `/books/view` (AppGateway.ts:21-22), so the gateway forwards it to `/api/apps/handoff?return=/books/view`. `appHandoffHttp.returnPathPattern` (line 14, `/^\/[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}\/(?:view\/[^\s]*)?$/`) does not accept `view` without a slash, so `serveAppHandoff` answers 400 (lines 51-57). The visitor never reaches the sign-in page. The same 400 happens for `/__halo/signin` without a `return`, because the gateway's fallback value `/` also fails the handoff pattern. Fix: share one return-path validator between both files, with the same URL-safe ASCII character set (which also removes the looser `[^\s]*`). Alternatively, normalize `/slug/view` to `/slug/view/` in the gateway before it builds the handoff URL. Then make the handoff accept, or substitute a safe default for, the gateway's fallback.

testRequests.target: Invited app: an anonymous browser GETs `${creator}/books/view` (no trailing slash), follows the redirect to /__halo/signin and on to /api/apps/handoff, and gets the 200 confirmation page; after it confirms and redeems the code, it lands on a /books/view path
testRequests.rationale: Checks that the gateway and handoff return-path validators agree for every path the gateway can generate, which the current tests do not exercise.
